Class WasmLanePool<W extends AutoCloseable>

java.lang.Object
de.christianmahnke.iiif.fliiifenleger.wasm.WasmLanePool<W>
Type Parameters:
W - The WASM module wrapper type (e.g. per-codec binding class).
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class WasmLanePool<W extends AutoCloseable> extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A fixed pool of WASM lanes for parallel execution.

A lane is one interpreter instance bound to one dedicated worker thread. WASM instances are neither thread-safe nor allowed to hop host threads, so each lane's instance is created lazily on (and used exclusively by) its own thread; tasks are routed round-robin across lanes. Separate instances are fully isolated (each owns its linear memory), which is what makes parallel execution sound — see the spike (WasmParallelSpikeTest history).

With a single lane this behaves exactly like the previous dedicated single-thread executors.

      public WasmLanePool(String threadNamePrefix, int parallelism, WasmLanePool.LaneFactory<W> factory, boolean ownsInstances)
      Parameters:
      threadNamePrefix - Worker thread base name ("<prefix>-<i>", or exactly prefix for a single lane).
      parallelism - Number of lanes; must be at least 1.
      factory - Creates one module instance per lane.
      ownsInstances - Whether close() closes created instances.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if parallelism < 1.
